question: What causes the intermittent unsupported_scan_motion rejection?
answer: The rejection is triggered by a single 1 ms discontinuity across joint, suspension and body state. The archived body command is two orders of magnitude too small to explain it. The event is aligned with a 10 cm collision-grid crossing, so contact generation / rigid constraint response is the leading subsystem; local slip or contact loss is not formally excluded without contact records.

run.outcome: FAULT CAMERA_unsupported_scan_motion on track 9 (the tenth) at simulation 754.648 s

fault_step.note: same-side front and rear disagree by 25-52 mm/s, which no rigid-body twist can produce

evidence: single-step isolated spikes occur 48-80 times per wheel per 2 s
spike rate 24-40 per second against 2.77/0.1 = 27.7 grid crossings per second
wheelbase 1.3 m is exactly 13 cells of 0.1 m, which is why all four wheels share an x phase
spike x phase is locked modulo 0.1 m
amplitude matches the mesh: largest slope discontinuity in terrain_5 yields 0.0059 m/s, observed background max 0.0023 m/s

collision_mesh_check.conclusion: the mesh at the fault location is a clean regular grid with no defect

leading_hypothesis: internal-edge contact artefact between the rigid wheel cylinder and the rigid triangle-mesh ground: the collision normal at a shared triangle edge is taken from the edge rather than the face, producing an impulse unrelated to the real slope. Consistent with every measured feature but not proven; contact normal, penetration depth and contact count would settle it and are still not recorded.
open: final per-joint velocity and steer commands are not archived at 1 kHz; the high-level body command is far too small to explain the event, but direct command/state comparison is still missing
tyre contact state and contact normal are still not recorded
residual statistics are not split by capture state, so the 418 over-limit samples cannot be attributed between turnarounds and scanning

normal_slope_input_is_insufficient.reading: The continuous height-profile slope does not directly explain the jump. This is not an upper bound on a rigid contact-constraint impulse and therefore does not exclude the triangle grid as the trigger.

fault_grid_alignment.reading: At 2.76 m/s the wheels reach the next longitudinal grid line in roughly one physical step. The fault phase lies in the same band as the background grid-locked residual spikes.

collision_detector_ab: results/collision_detector_ab.json: Bullet changes the signature but worsens stable capture residuals, so it is not adopted; the A/B supports contact generation as the controlling subsystem without proving the rare ODE outlier mechanism.

hypothesis_status.single_field_read_or_encoder_glitch: not supported: two drive joints change while suspension, steer and body velocity respond in the same step
hypothesis_status.normal_rigid_body_motion: ruled out: the four measured contact speeds cannot be represented by one rigid-body twist
hypothesis_status.high_level_control_command: ruled out at the recorded scale: body vx command changes only 0.000294 m/s while fr/rl contact speeds change 0.025/0.052 m/s; final per-joint command was not archived
hypothesis_status.local_slip_or_contact_loss: open: the record contains no contact state, normal, count or penetration depth
